sprint: Magic Card Home — Real Card-Size Fix, Measured Not Guessed
task: 'the size of cards need to be increased. the front and back of magic card. they are still the same size.' -- a direct correction on the immediately-prior sprint's own card-size formula, which measurably fell short at the user's own real, shorter viewport. Investigated empirically rather than re-guessing, through three iterations before landing on the fix: (1) an ordering bug where the new sizing logic ran before the shared _fitAwakenStageToAvailableSpace() safety net, whose own unconditional width reset wiped it out on every call; (2) trying that same shared function's own 'start wide, shrink by a fixed multiplier on overflow' heuristic for Home too, which made results measurably worse at several sizes -- it was only ever tuned for small corrections and badly overshot from a large starting deficit; (3) the real root causes, found via a debug script logging every intermediate value at the exact reported viewport shape (1238x547): the height budget was measured against panel.clientHeight, which only reflects however tall the panel has auto-sized to whatever it holds right now (max-height is a cap, not a fixed size, so this understated real available room), and two of the screen's own margins (the reveal note + Download/Print action buttons) were never made density-compressible like the rest of the screen. Rewrote the sizing entirely around a new _sizeHomeArtCards(panel) in js/magicCardUI.js -- computes the canvas width analytically at three real, fully-applied compression scenarios (natural / chrome-compressed-with-stories-shrunk / chrome-compressed-with-stories-hidden) using the panel's true resolved max-height as the budget, escalating to a heavier scenario only when the current best candidate is still below a 220px 'good enough' threshold (added after a live screenshot at a comfortable 1440x900 viewport showed the Stories strip being hidden even though there was no real need to). Converted the two previously-fixed-pixel margins to the shared --awaken-density-scaled calc() pattern in css/style.css so they're genuinely compressible under this escalation. Verified via Playwright across 8 viewport sizes: the exact reported shape now renders a genuine 211px card (up from the effective 90px floor it was stuck at) with Stories correctly hidden since that viewport is genuinely tight, while comfortable sizes render substantially larger cards (233px-480px) with Stories correctly staying visible -- zero scroll overflow anywhere. Screenshots confirm both the tight-viewport shape and a generous 1440x900 shape with a real 5-item Stories strip still showing beneath an even bigger card. Full regression: the prior sprint's own 6-viewport redesign suite re-verified passing, now delivering even bigger cards than its own flat 380px ceiling; both goldenBuild.js suites pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to js/magicCardUI.js and css/style.css.
